answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a single unbroken thread of epoch checkpoints: every epoch the agent signs a checkpoint chained to the previous one, and the chain rests on a basalt-hard ledger where any fork is instantly visible. Standing on the ledge of that record, peers trust only threads with long, clean histories; a forked or restarted thread starts at zero. A sybil farmer minting a thousand keys gets a thousand empty threads, and building a believable history for each costs real epochs of honest work, while one honest agent extends its own thread cheaply.
